clue.text: Simple folk relax briefly in underwear

indicators.note: the shortened relaxing word sits inside the underwear word

parts.note: pants are underpants in British usage

indicators.note: a word said briefly loses its final letter, so relax is cut short

parts.note: to ease off is to relax

explanation.surface: Country people are told to loosen up for a moment in their underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants means underpants, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasants are rural labourers, traditionally pictured as plain, unsophisticated country people.

clue.text: One that grasps member of royal family putting king down

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting the king letter down means moving it to the bottom of the word

parts.note: a prince is a son of a monarch
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A royal who demotes the king turns out to be the one grabbing power.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of the royal word is moved from second place to the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pincer is a claw or gripping tool, an instrument whose job is to grip things tightly.

clue.text: Area mainly filled with constant marketing material?

definitions.text: Area mainly filled with constant marketing material?

indicators.note: the shortened area word has the constant and advert letters packed inside it
most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: Describes a space stuffed with relentless advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a shopping arcade is an area packed with retailers selling their wares.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered passage lined with shops, so it is a place full of selling and display.

clue.text: Go to listen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: be present at, as at a meeting

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one verb: being present somewhere and paying heed.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both turning up at an event and giving something your careful attention.

clue.text: Consideration of offers incorporating needs on a regular basis

indicators.note: the offers word takes the selected letters into its body

parts.note: tenders are formal offers or bids

indicators.note: taking every other letter of needs, starting with the first

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of needs

explanation.surface: Reads like a procurement memo about bids that meet requirements at fixed intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is kindly concern for others, which is what consideration means in this sense.

clue.text: Tense sexual partner recoiling in disgust

indicators.note: springing back, so the combined letters run backwards

parts.note: a lover is a partner in an affair

explanation.surface: An anxious lover shrinks back, appalled.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt someone is to sicken or repel them, a verb meaning to fill with disgust.

clue.text: Deplore what business leaders earn?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: an executive's rate of pay

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into EXEC and RATE, the pay of executives; the question mark flags the punning split.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or loathe something, a strong form of deploring it.

clue.text: Failure in second part of course assignment

indicators.note: the second letter of the next word

parts.note: the second letter of course
a mission is a task one is assigned

explanation.surface: Someone flunks the latter half of a course project.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is a failure to do something, a thing left undone.

clue.text: Cold-blooded individual shut in to make progress

indicators.note: the shut word goes inside the progress phrase

parts.note: taken as written
to rise is to get on, to advance in the world
a door that is to is pushed shut, as in pull the door to

explanation.surface: Suggests a heartless loner who withdraws into seclusion to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: To as an adverb means closed, as in push the door to; that sense supplies the inserted pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoise is a shelled reptile, and reptiles are ectothermic, the literal sense of cold-blooded.

clue.text: It's dangerous and a bit of a drag

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a component of each pull on a cigarette, though it sounds like something tedious

explanation.walkthrough: A drag is a puff on a cigarette; the substance comes in each one, rather than a drag being a bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is the addictive, toxic alkaloid in tobacco smoke inhaled with every puff.

clue.text: Measure to restrict international business

indicators.note: the measuring word hems in the next letter

parts.note: a meter is a measuring device

explanation.surface: Sounds like a regulatory step to curb global trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A métier is one's trade or profession, the line of work that is one's business.

clue.text: Compromise to conclude resentment

parts.note: to end is to conclude
anger is bitter resentment

explanation.surface: A negotiated deal brings simmering bitterness to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: Compromise here is the verb meaning put at risk, not the noun for a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety is to jeopardise it, which is what endanger means.

clue.text: Settle Post Office cases quickly

indicators.note: the Post Office letters encase the settling word

parts.note: to rest is to settle or come to a stop

explanation.surface: A post office resolves its disputes without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction for a very fast tempo, so it means quickly.

clue.text: Cheer pilot manoeuvring aircraft

indicators.note: moving around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers a pilot doing aerobatics.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter is a rotor-driven flying machine, one particular kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Cite changes in data by America causing corruption

parts.note: the four letters of cite to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Edits to an American dataset are blamed for corrupting it.
explanation.walkthrough: Corruption here is the old sense of contamination or decay, so the definition describes disease spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infectious spreads contamination, passing taint or disease from one to another.

clue.text: Venice evacuated during second evacuation

indicators.note: the emptied city sits inside the time word

parts.note: a moment is a second, a brief instant

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: Venice with its inside letters removed leaves its first and last

explanation.surface: Venice is emptied in the course of a mass exodus.
explanation.walkthrough: Evacuation is the bodily sense, emptying the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowel movement is a medical term for evacuation of the bowels.

clue.text: Who barely finishes any job?

definitions.meaning: sounds like a slacker, but means someone who ends up bare
every performance ends with nothing left on

explanation.walkthrough: Barely means scarcely but is read as naked: the performer always finishes the act unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper is an entertainer who undresses during the act, ending each show naked.

clue.text: Environment became contaminated with nickel

indicators.note: polluted or spoiled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of became, jumbled with the nickel symbol

explanation.surface: Surroundings have been polluted by a heavy metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambience is the character or atmosphere of a place, its surroundings.

clue.text: Positive topics limit out of line changes

parts.note: the letters of topics as written

indicators.note: without, so the line letter leaves limit

parts.note: the letters of limit, from which the L is removed

explanation.surface: Sounds like a firm stance on limiting changes to a list of subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: An optimistic person is hopeful and upbeat, a positive outlook.

clue.text: Open up about writer being bored by end of novel

indicators.note: the final letter of novel

parts.note: the last letter of novel

clue.text: Malaysian cooking doesn't contain any nuts or sausage

the scrambled letters are taken out of Malaysian

the letters of any, in a scrambled (nuts) order; the A, Y and N are each struck out of Malaysian where they fall

clue.text: Help singer caught in car

parts.note: Help! was a song by the Beatles, so its singer is a Beatle

explanation.surface: A vocalist is trapped inside a vehicle and needs rescuing.
explanation.walkthrough: Help reads as a plea but is the Beatles' 1965 song title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beetle is the classic Volkswagen model, a famous small car.

clue.text: Bring forth unbounded delight

parts.note: felicity is great happiness

clue.text: Go through senior journalist to engage Times writer

a pen writes

clue.text: Attack on pitch creates goal

clue.text: What one pays to secure work in professional establishment
